item.title: Recent Advances in Optimization and Decision Making under Uncertainty: Theory and Algorithms
item.content:encoded:
Abdel Lisser, Paris-Saclay University

Jia Liu, Xi'an Jiaotong University

Francesca Maggioni, University of Bergamo

S. K. Neogy, Indian Statistical Institute

Vikas Vikram Singh, Indian Institute of Technology Delhi

This special issue invites theoretical and methodological contributions advancing optimization and decision-making under uncertainty. It seeks original research developing new optimization models, analytical results, computational methods, and convergence theories across mathematical optimization, stochastic optimization, robust optimization, game theory, and sequential decision-making.

The special issue is organized in conjunction with the International Conference on Operations Research: Theory, Applications and Emerging Technologies (ICORSI 2026) at Indian Institute of Technology Delhi. However, submissions are welcomed from all researchers in these areas regardless of conference participation, and all papers will undergo standard peer review.

Appel publié par Annals of Operations Research. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Mathematical programming
  • Convex, nonconvex, and mixed-integer optimization
  • Stochastic, robust, and distributionally robust optimization
  • Chance-constrained optimization
  • Variational inequalities and equilibrium problems
  • Game theory and multi-agent optimization
  • Markov decision processes and stochastic games
  • Reinforcement learning for sequential decision making
  • Online and data-driven optimization
  • Optimization under risk measures
  • Bayesian optimization
  • Black-box optimization

Timeline

  • March 31, 2028: Submission deadline

item.title: Climate Transition and Operational Risk Modelling: Implications for Supply Chains and Financial Decision-Making
item.content:encoded:
Andrea Flori, Politecnico di Milano

Anna Maria Gambaro, Università del Piemonte Orientale

Ioannis Kyriakou, University of London

Duc Khuong Nguyen, EMLV Business School

Climate-related risks threaten financial and economic systems through their effects on supply chains and firm operations. The transition to a low-carbon economy creates substantial uncertainty, particularly regarding timing and pace, destabilizing carbon-intensive sectors and triggering systemic challenges. This necessitates rigorous analytical methods to quantify climate risks and understand their propagation through interconnected economic systems.

Firms face tension between short-term profitability and long-term sustainability when transitioning to low-carbon operations. Supply chain vulnerabilities persist through global production networks where disruptions propagate, and financial markets transmit climate risks via asset prices and liquidity channels. This special issue welcomes operations research contributions using robust optimization, machine learning, and innovative analytical techniques to address how financial institutions and firms manage climate transition risks in portfolios and supply chains.

Appel publié par Annals of Operations Research. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Robust stochastic optimization methods for climate transition risks
  • Portfolio optimization and risk-adjusted return modelling under climate policy uncertainty
  • Credit and counterparty risk assessment under low-carbon transition scenarios
  • Risk-sharing mechanisms and insurance models for climate-related disruptions
  • Supply chain risk management in climate transition
  • Operational decision-making in emission trading schemes and carbon pricing
  • Predictive modelling of carbon stranding risk via supervised learning
  • Machine learning and big data analytics for climate risk scenario classification
  • Natural language processing applications in climate policy risk analysis
  • Bayesian network approaches to modelling climate transition risk propagation
  • Agent-based models of climate transition dynamics and systemic effects

Timeline

  • December 31, 2026: Submission deadline

item.title: Contextual Optimization with Side Information: Theory, Methodology, and Applications
item.content:encoded:
Stelios Bekiros, University of Turin

Andrea D'Ariano, Roma Tre University

Peng Wu, Fuzhou University

Guowei Zhang, Dalian University of Technology

Modern operations research integrates optimization with machine learning and statistics to incorporate side information—such as demand patterns and market conditions—into decision-making processes. This contextual optimization approach enables more adaptive and data-driven policies than classical optimization, though significant challenges persist including high-dimensional data, noisy observations, distribution shifts, and computational constraints.

The field requires new theories and frameworks that systematically combine learning and optimization under uncertainty, with emphasis on improving actual operational performance. This special issue invites high-quality contributions developing novel theories, models, algorithms, and applications addressing contextual decision-making using side information, spanning prescriptive analytics, adaptive algorithms, and real-world applications in transportation, supply chains, and healthcare.

Appel publié par Annals of Operations Research. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.
